recognize_zh: 兩顆成熟嗜中性球的細胞質布滿粗大、深紫色的毒性顆粒（toxic granulation），比一般嗜中性球淡粉紅的細顆粒明顯深而粗，符合嚴重感染時的毒性變化。
features: Two mature segmented neutrophils of normal size
Cytoplasm filled with coarse, dark purple-blue granules (toxic granulation) that are more prominent than normal neutrophilic granules
Nuclei with 3–5 lobes and condensed chromatin
Cytoplasmic vacuolation is subtle at most in this field; distinct Döhle bodies are not evident
Normochromic red cells with scattered platelets; no immature granulocytes in view
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two segmented neutrophils with abundant coarse, dark purple cytoplasmic granules, markedly more prominent than normal secondary granules, representing toxic granulation. Cytoplasmic vacuolation is subtle in this field and distinct Döhle bodies are not clearly seen. Red cells are normochromic, and platelets are present without clumping. Findings are consistent with toxic neutrophil changes, suggestive of a systemic inflammatory response such as sepsis in the appropriate clinical setting.

ddx.vs: Alder-Reilly granules are large, dark and present in all leukocyte lineages (including lymphocytes and monocytes) in a patient with mucopolysaccharidosis, independent of infection.
Growth factor therapy causes identical toxic-appearing granulation and Döhle bodies, distinguished by the medication history and often a left shift with myelocytes.
Chédiak-Higashi shows few giant, irregular fused granules rather than numerous uniformly distributed coarse granules.
Delayed processing causes vacuolation and nuclear degeneration without coarse toxic granulation; a fresh smear resolves it.
